title: M7.P5: Define category validation and explicit cloud actions

milestone.title: M7: pixelelated 0.0.1
milestone.description:
## Current priority — resolve the independent P5 audit findings

Independent review is complete: primary plus both approved Fable5.1/xhigh passes, with four confirmed findings (three Medium, one Low; no confirmed High/Critical). [#524](https://github.com/pixelelated/distribution/issues/524) owns the serial Phase7 resolution: PL-001 tracker reconciliation → PL-002 obsolete QA contracts → PL-003 safe localized path-refusal guidance and VM frames → PL-004 malformed audit-receipt handling. PL-001 corrections have exact readbacks: #497 closed completed against accepted185/187ARM handoff evidence; #510 preserves its open assembled-image adoption criterion. The sole audit owner `/root/m7_fresh_audit_owner` independently verifies each resolution before advancing. Frozen review input remains distro `ac64c80628ad6d5a69b803d82f186472529f7cd7` / ES `4e410dc9a816cc947f16235ad2b24824b29dd84e`; fixes are separate post-audit source. Both provider jobs have exited. No audit completion marker, firmware build or RC designation is claimed.

## Ordered implementation path — M7.P5

1. **#510 — settled post-rclone contract.** Link/retain the remote, then selected-category checks, explicit creation and local instructions. Preserve independent paths; no automatic move/follow. D-CLOUD-178/179.
2. **#515 — completed finite placement disposition**, with completed children **#520/#521** and runtime prerequisites **#522/#523**. Valid layouts stay in place; unsupported/ambiguous locations keep instructions. No demonstrable generic relocation mapping or repair API/screens is claimed.
3. **#508 — source integration complete; image inclusion pending.** The exact matched backend, native capture defaults/dependencies and ES pin are integrated. Canonical diagrams, screenshot indexes and complete retained receipts accompany the source.
4. **#507/#524 — active audit-resolution gate.** Primary and external grading are complete; resolve the four confirmed findings sequentially. Run primary and verified cross-lab blind/refutation stages under one continuous owner through the Facilitator. Exclude private device/cloud inventories and credentials; check the concrete new external payload's disclosure authority before dispatch. Do not replay candidate16's accepted audit or mutate the frozen scope.
5. **#508/#492/#344/#265/#359 — firmware and release.** Engineering GENERIC_X64 provides CF10 clean/public ROCKNIX adoption and final input inclusion; then affected H700 followed by SM8550 builds, source/licences, named physical smoke and release/publication gates. No RC designation yet.

**Owner device prerequisite #519:** controlled alignment and relevant residue disposition must complete BEFORE its next update transfer/reboot. Thirteen public-synthetic old-helper controls qualify, including pointer changes that bypass a transfer lock. Live recovery/startup-hook classification, exact reversible transaction/restart proof, named actions and state-bound acceptance remain open. This separate operational gate does not block common source/build/VM qualification. Unknown recovery data stays preserved; no personal cleanup ran.

**Parallel #511:** website/setup/ROM/BIOS guides remain separate; the Herdr lane awaits its explicit startup trust answer. Local instructions work without it.

## Current qualification

[Published source proof](https://github.com/pixelelated/distribution/tree/bc4ae05d30531516ebd19b6b167fc994f368c4c3/docs/qa-logs/2026-10-08-save-repair-cases): #520: 39 focused controls, 21 content and 30 validator regressions, nine actual-image BusyBox controls and ten reviewed affected UI frames (one rejected fixture retained). #521: 31 host controls versus four original failures; actual default/custom Guide+B rendered PNGs and normal installed saves-only backup/restore pass. All 38 preexisting synthetic cloud files and historical captures remain byte-identical. #522 explicit mode 0755 installation and #523 genuine target-built libcom_err resolve all 121 bundled ELF/plugins. Synthetic display output is not commercial gameplay/BIOS compatibility.

Root verified 196 cloud UI seals, 191 native UI seals, 469 host entries and two external references and complete preservation manifests. Final guest/provider/compiler/dependency scratch was retired after review; compact source/results/failure/log/frame receipts remain. No speculative guest or compiler is active. Source history052771f05d and ES4e410 are published, and 27 coordinated product paths are integrated in e6645cb5ea.

The earlier foundation remains qualified:1,311top-level host PASS, ordinary VM WebDAV and SFTP108PASS each, ES183cases/4,752assertions;99UI entries comprise89reviewed,nine rejected and CF10 pending. Source overlays are distinct from assembled-image/public adoption. Accepted candidate16 (15VMsuites,78screens,26RC2upgradechecks,318protocolassertions; eight #471 audit findings resolved) remains historical evidence.

Accepted H700/SP adoption and SM8550 artifacts stay historical inputs, not a second build queue. #492/#503/#506 retain terminal SM8550 evidence at frozen0553c0193a,737packages and bundle97367c3235fab7cc6d1ec2b54c390fe7ceff786612f29c9f177aaa288a33fb18. No Nova installation or new device action. Fourteen recipe-licence metadata gaps remain under the #344 component/source inventory gate; #359 owns branding terms and release-note linkage. D-INFRA-022 keeps only immediate-test disks/images and compact durable receipts; off-session delivery395, FOSSobservability432 and RAreset464 remain later work.

## Ordered critical path

| Phase | Priority / state | Exit gate |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **M7.P0 — Tracking conventions** | **COMPLETE** — tracking reconciliation #388; continuation/reference cleanup #389, with local checks and live readback. | This ordered body, open titles and canonical rules agree. No product readiness implied. |
| **M7.P1 — Safe migration and recovery** | **SOURCE GATE COMPLETE** — #365/#356/#320 plus #391/#392 source controls and guest promotion verified; all image-only acceptance stays assigned to P3. | Supported marker versions, repeatable numbered transitions, interruption/marker-failure recovery and settings-lock safety have passing/failing controls; applicable actor/state coverage is explicit. |
| **M7.P2 — Qualified release inputs** | **COMPLETE** — #361/#362/#386 input and unchanged-source preservation criteria reconciled; #310/#327/#332 software gates accepted. | Source manifests, actual consumers/runtime proof and explicit cut-time freshness evidence retained. |
| **M7.P3 — Build and qualify the image** | **COMPLETE FOR GENERIC_X64 CANDIDATE16** — all 15 default suites, 78 screens, 26 actual RC2 upgrade checks, and 318 protocol assertions; affected installed recovery/UI and exact unchanged-input carry-forward accepted. | Frozen product/input identity, preserved original state and independent completion/cleanup receipts. Device artifacts retain their own build/smoke gates. |
| **M7.P4 — Independent fixes audit** | **COMPLETE** — approved primary plus both Fable passes; all eight findings resolved in #471; repaired candidate 16 rebuilt and requalified. | Published audit 05/08/10 and exact checked/closed issue readbacks. No further external audit call required. |
| **M7.P5 — Device and release completion** | **IN PROGRESS** — #510 contract settled; #515 case disposition and source fixes qualified/published; #508 source integration complete; #507 independent delta audit is active before new firmware. Existing H700/SM8550 artifacts are accepted historical inputs. | Owner-reviewed public ROCKNIX adoption contract; qualified final inputs and firmware inclusion; source/licence/publication evidence and named physical smoke. |

### M7.P1 — Completed source work (migration portions superseded by #508)

1. **Migration controls and shared state model** — #365 with #356 and fixture correction #390: map applicable actors to T01–T26 assertions, preserve independent settings/content choices, and retain failing controls for the missed transitions. #391 owns inherited partial states; #392 owns missing-remote refusal.
2. **Versioned, repeatable migration** — #356: strict malformed/future-marker handling, numbered steps/journal, failure at tier or marker publication, safe retry and second-device follow. Name the actual older-build compatibility boundary; do not claim RC2 understands a future protocol.
3. **Settings recovery locking** — #320: deterministic concurrent-write and lock-busy controls, then fix stale recovery-record publication.

P1's historical source gate was subsequently qualified on candidate16. D-CLOUD-175/#508 now retires its cloud-folder move/follow engine; retain those proofs as history. Settings recovery locking and format safety remain required.

### M7.P2 — Work in order

1. **Current proxy with no functionality loss** — #361 and #384: reconcile local patches with current upstream, prove >100-game preparation, never count queued work as ready offline, preserve cached sign-in/data and queued base/subset awards through upgrade/reconnect.
2. **Compatible current dependencies** — #362 and #386: libsoup/WebKit build inputs plus glslang, SPIR-V headers, cbindgen and tllist; verified sources, compatibility and package checks. Coupled dependencies retain evidenced parent pins. Distribution ancestry remains frozen by D-WORKFLOW-111.
3. **Remaining software and execution gates** — #310 launch-memory cause/fix, #332 LED script/reselection, #371 push-hook fix, #367 process guard/help, #368 remaining handoff armatures. Diagnostic VM builds are allowed when required to investigate these.

#327's explanation-page source/frame/asset criteria are completed; public site publication remains P5. Upstream contribution #168 can proceed with qualified local fixes; upstream acceptance does not hold the candidate.

### M7.P3 — Work in order

0. **Lowercase pixelelated transition** — #409 identity source, sibling pins, cloud default, active addresses/policies and source controls are complete above. The RGB555 LCD asset system, Ocean splash/ES/theme integration and fresh input freeze are complete; candidate16 installed behavior proof is accepted. No RASTERATOPS predecessor gate. Repeat applicable qualification on new bytes; #409 is completed after final candidate 16 qualification and the P4 audit; old candidate evidence stays historical.

1. **Freeze, cold-build and retain the exact artifact** — #383/#344: distro/ES/splash commits, container digest actually consumed, source inventory, concurrency, fresh lowercase pixelelated root, logs, candidate manifest and digest verification before/after QA. #393/#394 provide corrected activity detection and automatic monitoring for future builds; the completed image keeps its frozen source. #395 retains disconnected delivery as an explicit outstanding infrastructure item; active-session supervision accompanies the durable watcher. A detached status file is not an alert.
2. **Clean install and RC2 upgrade; actual cloud paths** — #354 and #349/#350/#351/#352/#353/#363/#364/#365/#366/#376/#377/#379/#380/#381. Run full VM QA plus required opt-ins, local WebDAV/SFTP/MinIO-S3, independently reset promoted cases, pair migration, interrupted retries/future markers, writer-shaped archives, and injected failing controls.
3. **Preservation, performance and identity** — #361/#362/#384 runtime proofs; #310 memory/launch loops; #364 timing; #327 explanation frame/docs; #332 software fixture/UI evidence; #337 identity/manual update; #357 no upstream reporting; #359 licences. English/French at 640x480 and Nova1280x960, time-to-play and image brand/secret/localisation/source checks.

**Engineering-build gate is not the RC gate.** Image-only acceptance criteria must remain open until the image exists and supplies proof. They do not prohibit that engineering build. An RC claim requires the known software bugs resolved and P4 completed; no RC2 bug waiver carries automatically.

### M7.P4 — Work in order

The fixes review #383/#471 is complete, with all eight findings resolved on rebuilt and qualified candidate16. #375/#382 are the completed initial review and dispositions; do not restart any completed audit. Verified cross-lab receipts and installed resolutions remain retained. The general automatic version/depth policy is later #378, not a missing authorization for this review.

### M7.P5 — Work in order

The ordered path at the top is authoritative. #510/#515 source scope and #508 coordinated source integration are qualified/published. Remaining order: #507/#524 verified audit resolution → engineering GENERIC_X64 image and CF10 clean/public adoption → affected H700 then SM8550 builds → source/licence/physical/release gates. Completed source-overlay proof is retained; it does not close image-only criteria. The sole audit owner is active as recorded above; no new firmware build has started.


Historical device work: #502's EN/FR migration copy is qualified in ES5d2fcb9b/distribution0553 and the accepted SM8550 artifact. #504's authorized SP review found an incomplete owner migration; #505's extra diagnostic draft was superseded by #508 and closed not planned. Those results do not authorize resuming move/follow or require support for unpublished experimental states. D-CLOUD-175/178/179 replace that product flow with post-connection checks and explicit creation/actions.

The owner reports manually resetting experimental cloud state and requests separate read-only verification and a later one-time residue review (#516). Personal timestamps, paths and inventory stay private; the issue carries redacted conclusions only. This is not proof of reset device settings or a public adoption seed. No move/delete/sync is inferred and this operational task does not block common builds/VM QA. The owner's next handheld upgrade is separately gated by #519 (D-CLOUD-182).

#492 retains accepted H700 and SM8550 artifact history. After final qualified inputs are frozen, build and verify the affected firmware in the approved H700-then-SM8550 order, with per-image input/inclusion mapping. #265/#344 own release selection, corresponding source, notes/recovery/public documentation and manifest-bound assets; #359 owns branding terms and release-note linkage. Named physical smoke follows software qualification. No Nova deployment or new RG35XX SP action is inferred; retain each hardware fact and action's scope. No RC designation or publication until the applicable gates pass.

## Placement and historical references

M7-wide umbrellas: #383 delivery, #344 release contract, #354 cloud scope. Their titles omit P because they span phases. Other open titles use their owning M7.P phase. An input issue assigned P2 can retain image-only acceptance for P3; title placement does not waive that criterion.

The older #344 headings remain **contract sections**, not this execution queue: contract P0 is historical investigation; contract P1 spans current P2/P3 custody; contract P2 maps to current P3; contract P2b/P3/P4 map to current P5; contract P5/P6 are later work. Cite `#344 contract P2` explicitly rather than renumbering that evidence.

## Explicitly outside this release

Infrastructure topology/off-host restore drill (#347/#348/#355), replacement runner and progressive inherited-code review planning (#336/#339/#346), own telemetry design (#387), full site beyond the approved placeholder, trademark registration and general automatic review-depth policy (#378). Existing decisions D-WORKFLOW-102/113 and the release contract remain binding.


Build/VM QA OpenTelemetry evaluation is separately recorded in #432 following the maintainer's question. Existing device-telemetry design #387 is different. No collector/backend deployment or new RC gate inferred; current priority stays qualification above.

#432 remains backlog: D-INFRA-016 prefers fully FOSS observability, comparing SkyWalking and the clarified ClickHouse option with complete license/resource evidence and local-site/self-hosted online deployment, likely after separate build and agent/observer hosts are available. It is not an added M7 RC gate.

Hosted Dropbox/offsite observations are explicitly optional under D-QA-058/#462; #463 is milestone-less. No personal-cloud credential is a release dependency.

#464/D-QA-059 reopens automated dedicated RA fixture resets (Browserbase/Kitesurf/local browser comparison) as backlog; it does not delay this RC. #240 retains softcore route expansion and reset guidance.

#509/D-WORKFLOW-151 remains later active-name cleanup. #510/D-CLOUD-177/178/179 records the settled validator contract; #515 records the completed finite case disposition and its qualified coverage fixes. #511/D-WORKFLOW-152 owns parallel website planning, without a firmware release dependency. Linking or choosing a folder is not relocation consent (D-CLOUD-176).

#516 is a separate private operational reset/residue review, with no milestone or product cleanup feature.


Verification learning (#517, D-CLOUD-181): reusable offline byte/container controls are published and exercised in the completed coverage fixtures. They also inform #508 client-state/adoption assertions. Personal operational checks and later cleanup (#516) remain separate; #519 is the specific pre-upgrade gate. Independent save redundancy is deferred (#518).

body:
## Settled design and implementation ownership

The owner reaffirmed the post-rclone setup solution under D-CLOUD-179. This issue owns the settled contract and coordination. #515 and children #520/#521/#522/#523 are completed source qualification; #508 owns assembled-image inclusion and public adoption; #507/#524 own the active frozen-delta audit resolution. The ten-case review found no verifiable generic relocation mapping, so ambiguous placement retains instructions and explicit root selection. No repair API or screen is claimed delivered.

## Ordered implementation path — M7.P5

1. **#510 — settled contract and reference alignment.** Link/retain the remote, then offer category checks, selected folder creation and instructions. Preserve independent paths. D-CLOUD-178/179 settle this; do not ask the owner to choose the overall design again.
2. **#515 — completed finite save-layout disposition and qualification (children #520/#521/#522/#523 also complete).** Ten source-derived cases distinguish valid standalone layouts from ambiguous placement. No verifiable generic relocation mapping was found; unsupported locations keep instructions and explicit root selection. Coverage and native screenshot defects found during that investigation have qualified fixes. No automatic repair API/screens are implemented or counted as passed.
3. **#508 — source integration complete; firmware proof pending.** Integration `e6645cb5ea5ae3c7f699390a74b22d098fbeb7fb` contains qualified distro source `052771f05d841fb91fa818198f8f4e0ad83affb8` and ES pin `4e410dc9a816cc947f16235ad2b24824b29dd84e`. Automatic move/follow and startup/tidy paths are removed. Canonical references and source proof are published; assembled-image inclusion and public adoption remain open.
4. **#507/#524 — audit resolution active.** Independent primary review and both approved, verified Fable passes are complete. Resolve the four #524 findings under the serial Phase7 gate, including current-body reconciliation and actionable path-refusal guidance. The latter still needs its source/VM proof before the next pin. Candidate16's accepted audit is not replayed.
5. **#508/#492/#344/#265/#359 — assembled firmware and release gates.** Build the engineering image required for CF10 clean/public ROCKNIX adoption, map final inputs/inclusion, then finish source/licences and named physical/release gates. Source-overlay proof does not establish an installed RC.

**Parallel #511:** setup, ROM and BIOS guides and later verified QR destinations. Local instructions work without the website. The separate Herdr lane still awaits its startup trust answer; it is not a firmware gate.
## Current qualification

The check/create/instructions foundation has completed [source-overlay proof](https://github.com/pixelelated/distribution/blob/d5e2f78618624cad919afaba6784bef3f7eaf8c7/docs/qa-logs/2026-10-07-cloud-validator/ui/README.md) at distribution `6f89bc7cecee5972909828103689e2c7c0711c30` and ES `4e410dc9a816cc947f16235ad2b24824b29dd84e`. Qualified source `052771f05d841fb91fa818198f8f4e0ad83affb8` and ES `4e410dc9a816cc947f16235ad2b24824b29dd84e` are published; integration `e6645cb5ea5ae3c7f699390a74b22d098fbeb7fb` and proof `bc4ae05d30531516ebd19b6b167fc994f368c4c3` are on next. The integration manifest binds exact files, modes and aliases. #512/#513/#514 are qualified source fixes and closed; their firmware inclusion belongs to #508.

Evidence: 21 restore controls, 30 validator controls, 1,311 top-level host PASS (zero FAIL/SKIP), ordinary VM WebDAV and SFTP 108 PASS each; 99 UI-index entries comprising 89 reviewed frames, nine rejected frames retained and CF10 assembled firmware/public adoption pending. #512 unit logic passed 183 cases/4,752 assertions; later text-only fixes have separate compile/link/syntax/catalog/vocabulary proof. The prior foundation runtimes are retired and 529 sealed files retained; the subsequent #520/#521 guest and dependency scratch also completed qualification and were retired with compact receipts. Accepted candidate16/device artifacts and the 78-frame firmware baseline are unchanged. No new firmware build has started; #507 has completed its independent/external review and entered #524 resolution.

## Product contract

The [canonical flow, diagrams and evidence table](https://github.com/pixelelated/distribution/blob/next/docs/pixelelated/cloud-folder-flow-review.md) define:

- After connection, check selected categories, explicitly create selected folders/notes, change independent paths, or see instructions. Linking alone creates or relocates nothing. Category switches scope checks/creation; automatic sync has separate settings.
- Fresh defaults: `/pixelelated/Saves`, `/pixelelated/Backups`, `/pixelelated/Content`; ROMs under `<content>/ROMs/<system>`, BIOS under `<content>/BIOS`. Preserve existing configured paths until deliberately changed; a general arbitrary-layout browser is outside this first contract.
- Read-only bounded results distinguish present, missing, empty, recognized misplaced and unreadable within selected roots. They do not establish account-wide absence, complete transfer integrity or BIOS compatibility.
- A supported game-save/save-state/screenshot repair requires its own exact plan and confirmation. No blanket tidier, guessed destination or implicit ROM/BIOS/settings archive/game-content/unknown-file relocation.
- ROM/BIOS organization uses a computer/provider interface and useful local expected-path instructions. See instructions gains guide-specific QR only after #511 publishes verified destinations. Normal selective backup/restore and sync retain their separate purposes.
- Adoption starts from public ROCKNIX plus clean installs. The source-cited baseline is release20261001/tag `c445081a59518f37d9776e5412dd7b14910696f7`, with `/GAMES` and nested `/GAMES/backup`. Unpublished fork/PR states are historical, not public compatibility gates.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] The canonical review records the public release/tag and actual config/filter/package references, separated from unpublished experiments; see Who is upgrading in the linked flow review.
- [x] D-CLOUD-178/179 and the implemented diagram define selected-category checks/creation, independent paths and manual content guidance; prospective repairs are separately identified with #515 ownership.
- [x] Required flow/screenshot maintenance is published in both agent entrypoints, the canonical UI rule and evidence-index schema (D-WORKFLOW-155/156; f6037a9133). The final source-overlay CF01–CF15 table links reviewed happy/branch frames and explicitly pending CF10.
- [x] #515 records source-proven repair cases, exact preview/consent/count/bytes/collision/source-retention/stale-plan/interruption/verification contracts and qualified supported actions, or an evidence-backed unsupported disposition. No unsupported repair is counted as delivered.
- [ ] #508 final integration/adoption criteria are met on coordinated source and then actual assembled firmware; missing/unreadable and unrelated-file preservation remain proved. Coordinated source and pin integration are proved above; final image/adoption proof remains open.
- [x] Live M7, #508/#507/#515 and the canonical checkpoint agree on this implementation order and remaining gates; current audit-resolution reconciliation and exact complete-body readbacks are retained under docs/qa-logs/2026-10-08-m7-audit-resolutions/PL-001/; earlier b115af8d4c receipts remain historical. Personal review remains separate #516.

Can this be done on the VM? Yes: source-derived synthetic fixtures and GENERIC_X64 prove cloud setup, selected roots, applicable repairs, UI and clean/public adoption. No private Dropbox credential or physical-device action is needed. Current work is #524 audit resolution; source-qualified unchanged inputs are carried forward explicitly. Final CF10 adoption remains #508.

## Latest maintainer requirement — 2026-10-08

> I think we arrived at a good solution for this. I want to make sure everything we had is well documented, put into issues, and that we have a clear implementation path around using our project management methodology.
>
> I feel like we arrived at a good solution that relied on post-rclone remote setup. At the time, verification, directory creation, and user actions could live, so someone could help tidy up certain elements while we provide documentation for how to handle more data-intensive operations.
>
> This would also mean refactoring and redoing what we had done around the initial upgrade path, but I'm fine manually aligning myself with our new framework and directory structure. I can also revert the changes we made in Dropbox and then simply retitle the directory on my end.

## Owner-managed alignment and separate private review

The owner reports manually resetting the experimental cloud state and has requested read-only verification plus a later one-time residue review. #516 owns that private operational task, outside M7. Exact account history, timestamps, paths and object inventory remain restricted locally; the tracker records redacted conclusions only.

The report is not verified transfer integrity and does not establish reset device pointers. A later device test uses the new post-connection flow and named action authority; it does not resume the retired automatic migration. No move, deletion, sync or credential export is authorized by the read-only review. Public ROCKNIX/clean qualification uses independent synthetic fixtures and does not wait for personal cleanup.

## Earlier maintainer requirements (preserved verbatim)

> If we don't have it institutionalized already as a required process, we need to make sure that any time we make any change to EmulationStation or any part of our information architecture (or even screen content), we update the flow and then the accompanying screenshot for the flow. This is going to be increasingly critical as we work on automated testing.

> We also ensured that we updated all of our documentation and our diagrams that serve as canonical reference points for all of the flows and information architecture of the app. The idea was also to use these as a way to store screenshots at each flow, so we know what the definitive happy path flows are and also what the branching edge cases are. We have a visual benchmark and baseline for what the entire experience throughout EmulationStation is meant to be.

> Sounds good, and we should trigger a new lane if you want, within Herdr, for website work. I want to keep us focused here in this lane on the critical path of getting the build completed. We were in the flow, trying to get everything done. Run the changes and adjustments for the release candidate to simplify the experience and expectations of what happens when connecting a new remote via rclone, and I don't want to lose that progress and momentum.

> Also, with the "tidy up your cloud folders," that only mattered once they'd linked a cloud backend. We should respect their choice in doing that. If they happen to choose a different folder, I didn't think we would move their ROMs around. If we need to add more clarity to our own flows and what tidying up is, we should think more about that. Moving around ROMs, as we found, can be a very data-intensive operation, and so we might want to delineate between organizing or moving ROMs versus all of the other files we deal with. We're not finding ourselves in a situation where we're trying to use a handheld with a limited CPU to move hundreds of GB of files.

> But before we get too close and generate another build for a device, I want to review what our expectations are around reorganization, the flow, and how this works. For example, we need to think about if a user should be able to have their ROMs in a different directory or not. We could let the user select a different directory for their ROMs, or we could create the structure and instruct them to move their ROMs into the folder that's waiting for them.
>
> With the tidying up, we should think about what that does, because I actually don't remember right now if it touches ROM files at all and how it's currently structured or not. If we restrict it just to game saves, save states, and screenshots, that might be fine.
>
> Again, no one has used anything we've built, including what was opened as PRs to ROCKNIX, so they'll be coming from the current version of ROCKNIX. No one will be upgrading like I am, so we should not do anything to accommodate me. The only thing we should do is revert or clean up my folder after we attempted to do the migration from /ROCKNIX to /pixelelated.

> Well, another option is to create the folder and use it for the bits we enable. If they'd like to use it for ROMs, we should then make a decision about whether they would need to move their ROMs into that directory first or choose their own.
>
> For simplicity's sake, we might just say that once you link an Arcclone backend, we create the structure for them and then ask them to move things into those directories. All our tool does is give away that, once they've migrated the content in, it validates it. At that point, we could tidy things up because everything's already in the directory, so we shouldn't be moving anything around.
>
> Alternatively, we could offer strictly the tidy-up, save states, game saves, and screenshots. Another option would be to tell them what's not passing and have it be a series of checks. If they want to fix it, we could offer the option to fix that content type. This would be similar to what we do with the restore, where we let them choose from several options. We would just allow them to organize and let them select what they want to organize, and then the burden is on the user, not on us.

> Yes, this is where I think a validator is probably the way to go. Now we can offer a fix for smaller file types, and then we can deal with some edge cases that we know will likely happen. For example, if the ROMs aren't present at all, or if they're not in the right directory but present, I think the same would be true for the BIOS files. We can then also point them to look online for documentation on how to set everything up for those two types.

> A validator would also be helpful, and we may actually already have the building blocks in our restore and backup functions because we already have interface elements and checks around this.

> We also shouldn't have a link that is expected to be clickable. We could show a QR code, though.

> We need to build out our site, so this can be a future task we define now and tackle later. Once the site's live, we could have this on the wiki. It would take someone directly to the setup guide, and we could then have one for their ROMs and one for BIOS files. Instead of a fix button, it would say "See instructions" or something akin to that, and that would then show a QR code in a modal to take them to the page to fix it.


## Source-supported repair disposition — 2026-10-08

#515's ten-case review traces actual public ROCKNIX and packaged writers. For this finite set, ordinary standalone layouts remain valid; the historical extra-wrapper defect was in an unpublished fork and current path names cannot establish its provenance; flat saves/states/images lack unique system/core/media identity. Keep explicit root selection and manual instructions for ambiguous placement. No automatic relocation or repair screens are delivered or counted as passed. This is a bounded evidence-backed disposition, not a claim that a future proven repair is impossible.

The investigation identified actual coverage defects instead: #520 fixes save/content filter and bounded-validator handling for PPSSPP, DuckStation cards and Mupen64Plus states; #521 corrects DuckStation default screenshot placement while preserving custom paths and historical captures. #520 source1ee8e5199da0bc02e6aa4ebff94b951f5e8b4804 passes39focused real-rclone controls; 21content and30validator regressions, nine actual-image BusyBox controls and ten affected UI frames also pass. #521 has31host controls and actual default/custom Guide+B capture plus save backup/restore proof; #522/#523 supply executable permissions and target libcom_err closure. All five source tasks are closed completed, and their runtime scratch has been retired. The source table, primary writer references and compact receipts are under docs/qa-logs/2026-10-08-save-repair-cases/. The source is integrated under #508; assembled firmware/adoption remain open. #507 independent and cross-lab reviews are complete, with #524 findings now in resolution.

Owner-specific controlled alignment is #519/D-CLOUD-182 and must complete before the next test-handheld update transfer/reboot, using #516 residue dispositions. It does not block common synthetic proof or authorize private writes by itself.
